column11: derived: SNY turned 16.69% of revenue into free cash over 2023 to 2025 against the 25.5% its filed expense lines leave. Restated before interest: SNY paid 1,631mm EUR of interest inside operating cash flow over 2023 to 2025, 1.33% of revenue. The free cash flow above is struck after it and the valuation already charges the debt by subtracting net debt, so the charge falls by that much, from 10.45% to 9.12%. Checked at replacement capex: no plant depreciation on file for every year, and no amortisation line to take it out of the combined figure, so the charge stands. Checked without one-off cash: deal payments are booked under investing, so free cash flow never carried them, and no settlement or transition tax is stated for the window, so the charge stands. Left out: 350mm USD of legal settlement in 2025, printed only in USD, rather than converted. Restated without working capital build: over 2023 to 2025 SNY's cash flow statement shows receivables up 1,702mm EUR, inventories up 1,382mm EUR, payables up 1,445mm EUR, a working capital build of 1,639mm EUR, 1.34% of revenue. Growth ties that cash up once, not on every product for ever, so the charge falls from 9.12% to 7.53%. Struck on total revenue: Sanofi's filed cost lines sit against net sales of EUR 43,626mm and other revenues of EUR 3,090mm together (FY2025 20-F 0001628280-26-008403, Note D.34.2), so each ratio is scaled by 43,626 over 46,716 and charged on every revenue the model carries. The book's costs are the filed ones either way; this shares them across the revenue that earned them. Rebuilt on the book's own ratios on 0.3485 of the revenue they are struck on, against 0.2098 the filings leave as cash over 2023 to 2025 (free cash flow before interest, at replacement capex, without one-off cash and without working capital build), so the charge is 13.8760%.
